chunks: And Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, who said: Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn Al-Basri narrated to me, who said: Muḥammad ibn Sinān narrated to me from Bashīr Al-Dahhān, who said:

I used to perform Hajj every year, but I delayed for one year. When the following year came, I performed Hajj and visited Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him). He said to me: 'O Bashīr, what prevented you from performing Hajj in our past year?' I said: 'May I be your ransom, I had a debt owed to me by people and I feared losing it, except that I spent the day of ‘Arafah near the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' He said to me: 'You did not miss anything of what the people of the Stand (at ‘Arafah) had. O Bashīr! Whoever visits the grave of Ḥusain (peace be upon him) while knowing his right, is like one who has visited Allāh on His Throne.'

And from him, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn, who said: Ja’far ibn Muḥammad Al-Khuzā’i narrated to me from some of his companions from Jābir from Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), similar to it. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’ from his uncle from a man from Jābir, similar to it.
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of visiting the grave of Imam Husain compared to Hajj?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imām al-Ṣādiq (a.s.) elevates the Ziyārah of Imām Ḥusain (a.s.) to the status of Hajj, affirming that visiting his grave with *ma'rifah* (gnostic knowledge of his right) is equivalent to standing at ‘Arafah. This establishes the grave of the Imām as a spiritual axis (*mahwar*) where the believer encounters the Divine, reflecting the Shia concept of the Imām as the locus of God’s presence on earth.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari narrated to me from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn Al-Basri, from Muḥmmad ibn Sinān, from Bashīr Al-Dahhān who said:

I used to go to Hajj every year but one year I did not go. The following year, after going to Hajj, I went to Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)). Imam (a.s.) asked me, “O Bashīr! What prevented you from going to Hajj last year?” I replied, “May I sacrifice myself for you! Some people owed me some money and I was worried that I might lose it. So (instead) I spent the day of ‘Arafah next to the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.).” Imam (a.s.) said, “Then you did not miss anything compared to those who were in ‘Arafāt. O Bashīr! Those who go to the Ziyārah of the grave of Ḥusain (a.s.) knowing his rights are like those who have gone to the Ziyārah of Allāh on His Throne.”

The above Ḥadīth has also been narrated to me through the following chains: A) Muḥammad ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Ja’far Al-Ḥimyari, from his father, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥasan ibn Shammūn, from Ja’far ibn Muḥammad Al-Khuzā’i, from some of his companions, from Jābir (Al-Ju’fi), from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.). B) Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz, from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Muḥammad ibn Ismā’īl ibn Bazī’, from his uncle, from someone, from Jābir (Al-Ju’fi), from Abī ‘Abdillāh (a.s.).
